questions.question: Before changing lanes to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Check your left mirror, then look to the left.
Check your right mirror, then your left mirror.
Check your left mirror, then your right mirror.
Use your horn, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your left mirror, then look to the left.
questions.explanation: Always check the mirror on the side you're turning toward. Also turn your head and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: With a properly adjusted mirror, what can you see?

options.text: The lane behind you and part of the lane next to you.
Everything behind and to the side of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane behind you and part of the lane next to you.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors to see the lane behind you and as much of the lane next to you as possible. This helps you stay aware of traffic around you.

questions.question: When entering a curve, how should a group ride?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway. Staggered formation is best on straight roads.

questions.question: What is a problem with riding alongside another rider?

options.text: It allows you to maximize the surface of the road.
It allows you to communicate with one another.
It makes it easier for other motorists to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: It limits your escape routes.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another rider. This limits both riders' options to escape if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is slowing down by turning the engine off.
It is slowing down by downshifting.
It is not encouraged because it damages the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is slowing down by downshifting.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows you down, similar to using the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials at all times to stay visible.

questions.question: What lane position should you choose?

options.text: A position that reduces your space cushion and makes you visible.
A position that increases your space cushion and makes you visible.
A position that increases hazards and allows others to pass you.
A position that reduces hazards and lets you follow closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: A position that increases your space cushion and makes you visible.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that increases your space cushion and makes you visible. This helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, hazards, and provides an escape route.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not accelerate or brake during a wobble, as both will make it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and gradually close the throttle. Move your weight forward and down, and pull off the road as soon as possible.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash compared to riders with helmets.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets, regardless of speed.

questions.question: How much of your motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?

options.text: It should only be used on wet roads.
It should be the only brake you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent.
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about 70 percent of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Riding in cold weather for long periods could cause all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Hot flashes
questions.explanation: Cold weather riding can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: What is the only way to reduce the effects of alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects.

questions.question: In a normal turn, what should the motorcycle and rider do?

options.text: Lean together at the same angle
The motorcycle leans, but the rider stays upright
The rider leans, but the motorcycle stays upright

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean together at the same angle
questions.explanation: In normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest and is controlled by your left foot. Lift it with your foot to shift up to a higher gear. Press it down to shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake control usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot
questions.explanation: The rear brake is operated with your right foot.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chances of a crash?

options.text: Don't use turn signals when changing lanes
Watch only five feet ahead of your motorcycle
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible to others by using turn signals and your brake light. Keep a safe space around your motorcycle. Watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you. Always be ready to avoid hazards.

questions.question: What is the best way to brake in a straight line?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel
Use both the front and rear brakes while locking the rear wheel

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes without locking either wheel
questions.explanation: On a straightaway, use both brakes to stop in the shortest distance. Avoid locking either brake.

questions.question: How does braking in a turn compare to braking on a straightaway?

options.text: It is safe using only the front brake
It is safe using only the rear brake

questions.correctAnswerText: It is more difficult
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straightaway. You can use both brakes in a turn, but you must know the right technique and be very careful.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, how should you hold the handgrips?

options.text: Use a lot of throttle to get over the rough surface
Ride without a helmet so it doesn't cover your face

questions.correctAnswerText: Firmly to maintain control
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly when riding over rough surfaces to keep control of your motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a slippery surface?

options.text: Use the rear brake lightly while on the surface
Slow down before reaching the surface
Gradually speed up while on the surface
Downshift when you reach the surface

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before reaching the surface
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before reaching a slippery surface to avoid skidding. Be careful while riding on the surface.
